request.spec:
A steward can archive the sheet (a button; SHEET_ARCHIVED; anyone else is refused with an error
on the sheet). Show archived yes/no. On an archived sheet everything stays visible and every
change is refused with its usual error, including changing the sheet's today, every bulk action,
the paste box and the quick-add bar.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A steward can archive the sheet (a button; SHEET_ARCHIVED; anyone else is refused with an error
on the sheet). Show archived yes/no. On an archived sheet everything stays visible and every
change is refused with its usual error, including changing the sheet's today, every bulk action,
the paste box and the quick-add bar.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Stewards can now archive a sheet. On an archived sheet everything stays visible and every change is refused with its usual error. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec, the main archive test plus three longer scenarios.

**What's stored and how the server enforces it**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V46__sheet_archived.sql`, adds an `archived` yes/no column to the sheet table, defaulting to no.
- **Archiving:** a new archive endpoint in `SheetController` and `SheetService.archive`. Only a steward (including someone acting for one by delegation) can archive, and archiving an already-archived sheet is refused. A successful archive writes `SHEET_ARCHIVED sheet=<id> by=<user>` to the audit file.
- **Refusing changes:** a new `SheetArchivedGuard` refuses every change request on an archived sheet before it reaches its handler. That covers changing today, the paste box, quick-add, people, claims, rates and settings, so a refused change writes nothing to the store or the audit file. Reads and loading the sheet still work. It works the same way as the existing viewer guard.
- **Bulk actions:** these get past the guard on purpose. `ClaimBulkService` returns "0 done, all refused" for an archived sheet, which is how it already treats a viewer.

**Screen**
- The session bar shows `sheet-archived` (yes/no) and an Archive button (`sheet-archive`).
- If archiving is refused, the sheet's error (`sheet-error`) appears. It clears on the next archive attempt, change of today or sheet load.
- Every other form already showed its own error when the server refused it, so none of them needed changes.

There's no way to un-archive a sheet; the request didn't ask for one.
